newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: PSC Industries to buy shipbuilder stake.
newsitem.headline: PSC Industries to buy shipbuilder stake.

text.p: PSC Industries Bhd said on Wednesday it has agreed to buy the remaining 30 percent of Penang Shipbuilding & Construction Sdn Bhd it does not own from Business Focus Sdn Bhd for 205 million ringgit in cash.

In a statement, the ship-building and marine firm said it also entered into an agreement to acquire 50 percent of Suria Barisan Sdn Bhd for 28.32 million ringgit to be satisfied by an issue of 708,000 new PSC shares at 40 ringgit each. PSC is negotiating to buy the remaining 50 percent of Suria Barisan, which holds eight percent equity interest in privatised Naval Dockyard Sdn Bhd.
PSC said it is also negotiating to acquire Safe Era Sdn Bhd and Perstima Industries Sdn Bhd which together owns 40 percent of Naval Dockyard.

Penang Shipbuilding has a 40 percent stake in Naval Dockyard. PSC said the proposed acquisitions would enable it to consolidate and assume greater control over Naval Dockyard which is expected to contribute significantly to the long-term profitability of the group.
The privatisation of Naval Dockyard includes the building and delivery of 27 offshore patrol vessels to the Malaysian navy and the maintenance of the vessels for 15 years.

PSC said it has also entered into an agreement with J. Lauritzen Holdings A/S of Denmark to buy a 40 percent equity stake in Danyard Aalborg A/S and a 48 percent stake in Danyard A/S for 250 million ringgit in cash.
The Danish companies are involved in building commercial and navy ships. As part of the acquisition, the companies have agreed to provide technology transfer to Penang Shipbuilding.
PSC is controlled by Malaysian businessman Amin Shah, who also heads Business Focus.
In the same statement, PSC said it had terminated a preliminary agreement with Usahasama Timur Barat Sdn Bhd to develop new power facilities in Kazakhstan.
The pact for the $866 million turnkey contract was signed with Usahasama in July. PSC said the pact was being rescinded because Usahasama had requested a termination.
